_comment: Mutation testing: the layer that tests the TESTS. It edits the source in small ways — flipping
a >= to a >, deleting a branch, changing a constant — and reports which edits the suite failed
to notice. A surviving mutant is a behaviour nothing pins.
AN AUDIT, NOT A GATE, and deliberately not in `npm run check`. It takes minutes rather than the
gate's seconds, and a hard score threshold is a number that eventually gets lowered to make a
commit land. Run it, read the survivors, fix what matters, move on:  npm run mutate
A hand-run sweep of ten mutants before this was configured killed all ten — but each died to
exactly ONE test, so every behaviour rests on a single assertion. That is what a full run is
for: finding the same fragility everywhere rather than in the ten places someone thought to look.
